title: Steve Martin's 'Meteor Shower' Runs at American Stage in St. Petersburg Through Nov. 22

content:
Steve Martin's comedy Meteor Shower takes the stage at American Stage in St. Petersburg from Nov. 4 to Nov. 22. Of the 18 shows on the calendar, a few are close to selling out, according to I Love the Burg.

All shows happen at the Raymond James Theatre, 163 3rd St. N. Adult humor earns it a 16+ rating.

Norm and Corky invite new friends Gerald and Laura over for dinner. The plan is simple: the four will watch a once-in-a-lifetime meteor shower. Then the meteors streak overhead, the cocktails keep flowing, and the night slides into chaos as reality bends and good manners fall away.

At its core, the story deals with marriage, desire, and the pull that draws people together and then tears them apart. Critics have called the show "bold, witty, delightfully unpredictable, and just the right amount of absurd."

Anthony Gervais, a longtime American Stage director, leads the production. Martin wrote the play.

Meteor Shower first hit Broadway with Amy Schumer and Keegan-Michael Key in the lead roles. It marked the Broadway debut for both stars. Since its Broadway run, the play has been staged by theaters around the country.

Performances run Wednesday through Sunday. On Saturdays, audiences can pick a matinee or an evening show.

Two dates come with extras. On Thursday, Nov. 12, the cast and crew stay after the show for a talkback. Saturday, Nov. 14, is ASL Night.
